alert: Postgres pooled connections exhausted; checkout requests returning 503
logs:
2026-01-05T01:18:03Z payments-api-6c8d7f5b9-m2xkq ERROR db.pool - timeout acquiring connection after 30000ms
2026-01-05T01:18:04Z payments-api-6c8d7f5b9-r7vnc ERROR sqlalchemy.pool.impl.QueuePool - QueuePool limit of size 20 overflow 10 reached
2026-01-05T01:18:07Z pgbouncer-7f6c89c6d8-pq2lm LOG client_login_failed: pool checkout exhausted
2026-01-05T01:18:12Z checkout-service-5b77d8c4f9-j8tps ERROR postgres - remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections
2026-01-05T01:18:18Z payments-api-6c8d7f5b9-m2xkq WARN request failed status=503 path=/v1/payments latency_ms=30012
root_cause: The nightly batch job consumed most available pooled database connections and left pgbouncer unable to satisfy application connection requests.

actions.step: Scale payments-api and checkout-service pods to add capacity.
Raise the PostgreSQL max_connections setting to temporarily increase capacity.
Restart pgbouncer and pause the nightly batch workload so pooled connections can recover.

postmortem: The nightly batch exhausted the available connection pool and application scaling increased connection demand instead of relieving it. Restarting pgbouncer after pausing the batch restored normal pool utilization.

root_cause: The self-hosted Redis primary became unavailable while a healthy replica remained available for promotion.

actions.step: Restart the Redis Sentinel process and wait for automatic recovery.
Promote the healthiest replica manually to primary.
Update the service endpoint to target the promoted primary and restart affected application pods.

postmortem: The self-hosted primary became unreachable and automatic Sentinel recovery did not restore service quickly enough. Manual replica promotion followed by an endpoint update restored application connectivity.

root_cause: An abandoned inactive replication slot prevented WAL recycling and filled the PostgreSQL data volume.

root_cause: PayFlow experienced elevated response latency, causing the configured client deadline to expire on payment requests.

actions.step: Increase the payments-api client timeout from 5 seconds to 20 seconds.
Enable exponential backoff retries together with the gateway circuit breaker.
Fail over payment traffic to the secondary gateway endpoint.

postmortem: PayFlow response times exceeded the application deadline and caused a burst of payment failures. Backoff with circuit protection reduced pressure on the dependency, and secondary gateway traffic restored payment processing.

root_cause: A mass expiry event emptied the cache tier and caused many identical requests to hit Postgres simultaneously.

actions.step: Increase the cache tier capacity to absorb the sudden miss volume.
Add read replicas to distribute the increased backend query load.
Enable TTL jitter and request coalescing to prevent concurrent cache rebuilds.

postmortem: A synchronized expiry caused a cache stampede and sharply increased database reads. More capacity did not remove the duplicated work, while TTL jitter and request coalescing reduced the backend surge.
